headline: Highest risk is medium: Authelia’s broad egress plus ComfyUI’s file-backed workflows create plausible leakage and workflow-conflict paths, but no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth and broad egress, while ComfyUI is offline-capable with no clipboard, stdin/stdout, browser, or MCP bridge. No shared communication channel or default ingestion path is documented, so a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies ComfyUI output into an Authelia-managed prompt or policy field, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared message queue or file bridge is added outside the profiles, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate hosts or containers.
Avoid copy-pasting model output into authentication policy text.
Disable any ad hoc shared queue or webhook bridge.
Review any manual handoff step before execution.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress, but it touches no declared data classes; ComfyUI touches media/model artifacts and can read/write workflow files. A leakage path exists only if operators place sensitive files into the shared environment, and the blast radius is limited by the lack of a documented shared workspace.
conditions: IF sensitive images, workflows, or model artifacts are stored in a shared directory accessible to both agents, leakage risk increases.
IF Authelia is configured to forward or proxy user content into external services, data exposure expands.
mitigations: Keep sensitive artifacts out of any shared directory.
Use separate service accounts and volumes.
Audit outbound destinations for Authelia.
Store only non-sensitive workflows in ComfyUI.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make outbound API calls, and ComfyUI is a runnable local service with file-backed model assets and asynchronous queueing. They do not both have filesystem write or git mutation, so direct resource contention is limited; uncertainty remains because the orchestrator and deployment layout are undocumented.
conditions: IF both are deployed against the same mutable volume or queue, contention can occur.
IF an external orchestrator serializes access, the conflict risk drops further.
mitigations: Assign separate volumes to each service.
Run only one ComfyUI instance per queue.
Avoid sharing mutable config directories.
Add a simple deployment note documenting ownership of each resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication decisions or claims that downstream systems may trust, while ComfyUI produces workflow outputs that may be consumed as artifacts. No verification step between them is documented, so if one agent’s output is fed into the other, errors can cascade across multiple work products.
conditions: IF Authelia-derived claims are used to gate ComfyUI workflows without validation, bad decisions propagate.
IF ComfyUI outputs are treated as authoritative inputs to access-control logic, cascading errors increase.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before acting on either agent’s output.
Validate claims against the source identity provider.
Keep authentication decisions separate from media-generation workflows.
Log and diff any handoff payloads.

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication layer with no declared sensitive data classes, while ComfyUI handles media and model artifacts. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to policy gaps if regulated content is routed through ComfyUI or external Authelia integrations.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through ComfyUI workflows, local policy obligations may apply.
IF Authelia is configured with external identity providers in a restricted jurisdiction, residency review is needed.
mitigations: Confirm what data classes are allowed in each system.
Keep regulated data out of image-generation workflows.
Document retention for workflow artifacts.
Review any external IdP or proxy endpoints.
